react_result.final_narrative_text: A multi-paradigm metabolomics analysis of seven differentially abundant metabolites identified a single dominant biological signal: extensive perturbation of the arachidonic acid cascade and eicosanoid synthesis network. Across three independent analytical paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (WikiPathways/SMPDB), Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the same five eicosanoid intermediates consistently achieved the top ranks with extremely low FDR or p-values. The WikiPathways pathway 'Eicosanoid synthesis' (WP:WP167) ranked #1 in RaMP with FDR = 6.84×10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment = 1429.7, with all five arachidonate-derived metabolites (5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A₄, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂, arachidonic acid) present as hits within a 27-member canonical roster. Mummichog independently ranked 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its top hit (p = 4.20×10⁻⁴, overlap = 11/11 compounds), and MetaboAnalystR confirmed KEGG:hsa00590 as its top pathway (score = 1.0, 4 of 44 pathway members hit). The two non-lipid metabolites — glycolaldehyde (C00266) and losartan (C07072) — did not contribute to these pathway hits; glycolaldehyde appeared only in peripheral Mummichog hits for glycerophospholipid metabolism and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, while losartan did not appear in any ORA or network hit. Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the obligate substrate: it is oxygenated by 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) to produce 5-HETE and leukotriene A₄, and by 15-lipoxygenase (ALOX15) to produce 15-HETE; 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ arises from non-enzymatic dehydration of prostaglandin D₂. The convergence of five structurally diverse eicosanoid derivatives across three independent methods provides robust evidence that the treatment group experiences significant perturbation of the arachidonic acid oxidative cascade, consistent with cyclooxygenase or lipoxygenase pathway modulation.
